Convert CMYK values to a HEX color

Source: R/cmyk2hex.R
cmyk2hex.Rd

Converts cyan, magenta, yellow, and black (CMYK) color values into a six-digit hex triplet.

Usage

cmyk2hex(c, m, y, k)

Arguments

c

a numeric for cyan channel intensity, between 0 and 100.

m

a numeric for magenta channel intensity, between 0 and 100.

y

a numeric for yellow channel intensity, between 0 and 100.

k

a numeric for black channel intensity, between 0 and 100.

Value

A character string containing a six-digit hex triplet in the format #RRGGBB.

Details

CMYK values are expressed as percentages, ranging from 0 (no ink) to 100 (maximum ink coverage). This function handles the conversion to proportions.

Conversion to RGB format is performed using a simplified mathematical model, in which the CMYK values are first converted to proportions between 0 and 1. The resulting RGB values are calculated as:

$$ R &= 255(1-C)(1-K) \ G &= 255(1-M)(1-K) \ B &= 255(1-Y)(1-K) $$

The resulting RGB values are rounded to the nearest integer before being converted to a hex triplet.

This conversion is an approximation and does not account for printing conditions, ink characteristics, paper properties, or ICC color profiles. Consequently, the resulting hex triplet may differ from color-managed CMYK-to-RGB conversions, particularly when CMYK values originate from professional printing standards. If you are presented with a CMYK value and an RGB value for the same branded color and want a hex triplet from it, use rgb2hex() instead of this for obtaining the hex triplet.

Examples

cmyk2hex(100, 69, 8, 54)
#> [1] "#00246C"
cmyk2hex(99, 51, 8, 36)
#> [1] "#025096"
cmyk2hex(0, 0, 0, 0)
#> [1] "#FFFFFF"
